text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Netherlands will continue to assist Bosnia through donations and the World Bank's projects in response to priorities set down by the Bosnian goverment, Jan Pronk, the Dutch minister for development and cooperation said. He added during a visit to Sarajevo that his government will decide on the total amount of aid to Bosnia shortly before a donors' conference scheduled for March 4 in Brussels.
- Bosnian foreign trade minister tells a news conference that Bosnia asked the Netherlands for assistance in paying off loans from the World Bank and to grant bilateral assistance.

- The total amount needed to reconstruct water supply facilities in Bosnia is estimated at $950 million, deputy minister for water management, agriculture and forestry of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation government tells a news conference.

- The Bosnian gas supply company Energoinvest-Energopetrol and Russia's Gas Export company sign a contract on three-year gas supply to Bosnia but first it has to pay $12.3 million debt for the gas spared by the Bosnian Serb Republic, Energoinvest's deputy manager tells a news conference.

- The success or failure of the Sarajevo cantonal government will be measured by the number of employed citizens, co-chairman in the Bosnian Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic says after attending a government session.

- Installation of 300 public telephone booths, of which 100 are in Sarajevo, will begin in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation in February for the first time since the end of war, the state postal company says.

- Current vice-president of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation will remain at the post while the new federation president will be former federal defence minister Vladimir Soljic, a Croat, daily cites its sources as saying.
- Special U.S. envoy for economic development in Bosnia, Richard Sklar, will leave Bosnia by the end of February, diplomatic sources tell the daily.

- Turkish Euro Capital bank will soon open an office in Sarajevo with a starting capital of 15 million deutsch marks, the bank officials tell co-chairman of Bosnia's Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic.
